article_content: Manchester City's pursuit of their first English Premier League title in 44 years has encountered another obstacle after they were held to a 3-3 draw by Sunderland at the Etihad Stadium. Despite the setback, Roberto Mancini's team managed to preserve their unbeaten home record in the league. However, this result means that their rivals, Manchester United, will have the opportunity to extend their lead at the top of the table if they secure a win at Blackburn Rovers on Monday. The match saw Sebastian Larsson put Sunderland ahead after 30 minutes, but Mario Balotelli equalized from the penalty spot just before the break. Nicklas Bendtner then headed home in first-half injury time to put Sunderland back in the lead, but City fought back with two goals in two minutes, courtesy of Balotelli and Aleksandar Kolarov, to claim a point. Meanwhile, Chelsea's quest for Champions League qualification received a significant boost as they defeated Aston Villa 4-2 at Villa Park. The win was especially poignant given that Villa captain Stiliyan Petrov, who was recently diagnosed with acute leukemia, watched from the stands and received a standing ovation before the game. Branislav Ivanovic scored twice for Chelsea, while Fernando Torres sealed the win with a goal in injury time. Arsenal's winning streak came to an end as they lost 2-1 to Queens Park Rangers at Loftus Road, with Adel Taarabt and Samba Diakite scoring for the home side. Elsewhere, Everton moved above Merseyside rivals Liverpool with a 2-0 win over West Bromwich Albion, while Wolverhampton Wanderers' poor form continued with a 3-2 loss to Bolton.
